items.topic: Indicate study design with commonly used term in title or abstract
Informative and balanced summary of what was done and found
Scientific background and rationale for investigation
Specific objectives including prespecified hypotheses
Key elements of study design presented early in paper
Setting, locations, and relevant dates (recruitment, exposure, follow-up, data collection)
Cohort: eligibility criteria, sources, methods of participant selection and follow-up
Cohort (matched): matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed
Clearly define outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, effect modifiers, diagnostic criteria
Data sources and measurement details; comparability of assessment methods across groups
Efforts to address potential sources of bias
Explain how the study size was arrived at
Handling of quantitative variables and rationale for groupings
All statistical methods including those used to control for confounding
Methods used to examine subgroups and interactions
How missing data were addressed
Cohort: explain how loss to follow-up was addressed
Describe any sensitivity analyses
Numbers of individuals at each stage (potentially eligible, examined, confirmed, included, followed up, analysed)
Reasons for non-participation at each stage
Consider use of a flow diagram
Characteristics of study participants and information on exposures and confounders
